title: Add a machine to the hub
goal: The machine's bridge is enrolled and passes a test call

steps.title: What the bridge is
steps.text: The bridge is one small program on your machine. It only dials out to this hub, opens no ports, sends no telemetry, and runs every command inside the OS sandbox for the access you approve.

steps.title: Create an enrollment code
steps.text: In the hub, open Machines, choose Add machine, pick a label, the OS and shell profiles. Copy the one-time code; it lasts 10 minutes and works once.

steps.title: Get the bridge for this OS

text_by_os.linux: Download devagotchi-bridge for Linux from devagotchi.com and check its checksum.
text_by_os.macos: Download the signed Devagotchi bridge for macOS from devagotchi.com and check its checksum.
text_by_os.windows: Download devagotchi-bridge.exe from devagotchi.com and check its checksum.

steps.title: Enroll with the code
steps.text: Run this and paste the code at the prompt (not as an argument, so it stays out of your shell history).
steps.changes: Writes bridge.toml and a 0600 token file in the bridge config folder
steps.check: The hub shows the machine as enrolled

steps.title: Start the bridge
steps.text: Run it in the foreground now, or install it as a user service with the install command.

steps.title: Also enroll WSL (Ubuntu)?
steps.question: WSL becomes its own machine with its own grants. Enroll it now?

steps.title: Enroll WSL as its own machine
Enrolled
steps.text: The machine is enrolled. It shows online only after a real call succeeds. Agents still need your approval for every kind of access.
